clue.text: State where girl is sanctimonious about small drink

indicators.note: the girl, is and sanctimonious pieces go round the small drink, holding it between them

parts.note: miss is a title for a girl or young woman
pi is informal British for sanctimonious, short for pious
a sip is a small mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: Someone observes that a prim young woman's home state frowns on even a little tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: The small drink sits between the S and the P. 'Pi' (pious) is a common crossword word for smug or sanctimonious.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty United States, in the Deep South along the great river of the same name.

clue.text: Scot with joint, not good? Artificial device needed

parts.note: Mac is an informal way of addressing or naming a Scotsman

indicators.note: not good tells the solver to take the letter for good out of the joint

parts.note: a hinge is the joint on which a door swings

explanation.surface: A Scotsman with a bad knee wonders whether some artificial aid is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mac' is a casual, rather dated form of address for a Scotsman; 'not' strips the good out of the joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical contrivance or apparatus built to do work is a man-made device.

clue.text: Cut first sign of laziness in band

indicators.note: in places the opening letter of laziness inside the word for band

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn round the waist or over the shoulder

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A band sacks a member at the first hint of idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: To slash is to cut with a sweeping stroke, so the noun is a long cut.

clue.text: It drives mischief-maker and soul in play

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous sprite

indicators.note: play here suggests the letters of soul and in being moved about freely, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prankster and a sensitive soul take part in a stage play, apparently driven by something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In play' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is part of the anagram fodder and 'play' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Impulsion is a driving force or impetus, the thing that pushes something forward.

clue.text: One that's wise to contemplate — not half!

indicators.note: not half means the first half of the word for contemplate is dropped

parts.note: to envisage is to contemplate or picture something in the mind

explanation.surface: A wise person is advised to think things over, and the reply is an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' (also British slang for 'very much') removes ENVI, the first four of ENVISAGE's eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sage is a person of profound wisdom, revered for sound judgement.

clue.text: Affected manner disrupting centre in exercises

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled letters inside the abbreviation for exercises

parts.note: PE is physical education, gym exercises at school

indicators.note: disrupting suggests the letters of centre being thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone's affectations upset the atmosphere at the heart of a fitness class.
explanation.walkthrough: PE (physical education) is the British school name for gym lessons; 'disrupting' scrambles centre and 'in' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretence is a false show or affectation, behaviour put on to impress.

clue.text: Stupid lot in china needlessly

indicators.note: lot in says a batch of letters sits within the words china needlessly

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a whole set of crockery bought for no reason was a foolish purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly, senseless or lacking any sense.

clue.text: Beautiful plant pruned

indicators.note: pruned means the plant's name is cut back, losing its final letter

parts.note: angelica is an aromatic plant whose stems are candied for cakes

explanation.surface: A gardener admires a lovely plant after trimming it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pruned' removes the last letter from ANGELICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic means like an angel, lovely or pure in looks.

clue.text: Light backing for service held by energetic figure

indicators.note: held by means the reversed service sits inside the energetic figure

parts.note: a goer is a lively, energetic person

indicators.note: backing for means the word for service is read backwards

parts.note: Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: Someone lively provides a little support for a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like a noun or verb but is the adjective; 'backing for' turns the church service round and 'held by' puts it inside the lively person.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is fine filmy cobweb, and so anything very light and delicate.

clue.text: Winner woman snubbed for glamorous drink

parts.note: a champ is a champion, a winner

indicators.note: snubbed suggests a snub nose, cut short, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Agnes is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A champion ignores a woman and reaches for some fizz instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snubbed' plays on a snub nose, short at the end: the woman's name loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is the sparkling wine of celebration and luxury, the classic glamorous tipple.

clue.text: Some unofficial on-goings in company

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Unauthorised goings-on are happening among the staff of a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming along with someone means accompanying them, being in their company.

clue.text: Take in popular tipple around hotel

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ale is beer, a tipple

explanation.surface: Someone samples a favourite drink at a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhale is to draw air or smoke into the lungs, to breathe it in.

clue.text: Setback with exhibit swamping royal society

indicators.note: swamping means the exhibit word engulfs the abbreviation for royal society

parts.note: to reveal is to show or exhibit

explanation.surface: A scientific display overwhelms the Royal Society, a blow to its plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swamping' means the word for exhibit engulfs the Royal Society's initials, Britain's national science academy.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal is a change of fortune for the worse, a reverse or setback.

clue.text: Flatterer gaining attention with judge

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention
a wig stands for a judge, who wears one in court

explanation.surface: A sycophant wins the attention of a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: An earwig is an old word for a flatterer who whispers privately in someone's ear, as well as the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Earwigging is pestering someone with private talk to sway them, so the word came to mean a toady or whispering sycophant.

clue.text: Aggression in an estate after a scrape?

definitions.text: Aggression in an estate after a scrape?

parts.words: Aggression in an estate after a scrape?
parts.note: estate suggests property, but here it is an estate car; the fury is a driver's after a minor collision

explanation.surface: Neighbours on a housing estate fall out after some minor scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is the British name for a station wagon, so the aggression is between motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists' violent fury at other drivers often flares after a small bump between cars.

clue.text: Fellow of no practical importance

definitions.meaning: a fellow is a member of a university's teaching staff, a scholar
a point is called this when it is purely theoretical and irrelevant in practice

explanation.surface: A college fellow is dismissed as irrelevant in the real world.
explanation.definitionFit: A university don is a scholar, and a merely theoretical question is a moot or irrelevant one.

clue.text: Native Caribbean brother?

definitions.meaning: someone from Dominica or the ... Republic, both in the Caribbean
a friar of the order founded by St Dominic is a Black Friar, a religious brother

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a West Indian is a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a person from those island nations and a friar of the Order of Preachers.

clue.text: Superficially attractive item vaguely caught south of island

indicators.note: in a down answer south of means the following letters are placed below the island

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is a Greek island

indicators.note: vaguely suggests the letters of item are arranged loosely, in no fixed order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A holiday item picked up on an island turns out to be merely pretty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vaguely' scrambles item; in a down entry 'south of' means the scrambled letters come below the island, with the cricket C last.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic means affecting only the surface appearance, improving looks without deeper change.

clue.text: Very clever chap getting support at home before case

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
to be in is to be at home
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A bright fellow is given help at home before going to court.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainbox is an informal word for an exceptionally intelligent person, a genius.

clue.text: Cell, where eggs are found?

definitions.meaning: an electrical cell, the source of power in a torch
in ... farming hens are kept in rows of cages to lay eggs

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a prison cell is the place to look for eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a power cell and a set of cages for intensively farmed laying hens.

clue.text: Love song again appearing in middle of date

indicators.note: appearing in means the word for again turns up inside the middle letters of date
the middle of date is its two central letters

parts.note: more can mean again, as in once more

explanation.surface: A love song is played again in the middle of a romantic evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of' takes the two central letters of date, and 'appearing in' slips the word for again between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoret is an old word for a love sonnet or love poem, a romantic lyric.

clue.text: Revolutionary officer among wild trees getting support

indicators.note: among means the reversed officer sits within the scrambled trees
wild suggests the letters of trees being thrown into disorder
revolutionary means the officer's abbreviation is turned right round

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for a lieutenant, an army officer

explanation.surface: A rebel officer hides in a forest and gets some backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' scrambles trees; 'Revolutionary' turns the lieutenant's abbreviation round, and 'among' sets it inside, just before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame holding up a table top, a support.

clue.text: Irritating remote is malfunctioning

indicators.note: malfunctioning suggests the letters of remote and is going haywire into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the TV remote control keeps playing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link word, but it is part of the anagram fodder with REMOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome is annoying or wearisome, getting on one's nerves.

clue.text: Drug that's positive in origin

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for positive inside the word for origin

parts.note: a seed is the origin of something, the germ from which it grows

explanation.surface: Someone says a drug's beginnings were positive.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed is slang for amphetamine, a stimulant.

clue.text: Call for more action on boards?

definitions.meaning: a shout from an audience asking a performer to carry on
the boards are the stage, so this is an extra performance given there

explanation.surface: An audience wants more stage action.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the audience's demand for another number and the repeat performance itself.

clue.text: African native certainly followed by an investigator

parts.note: OK means certainly or yes
an is the indefinite article, here giving its shorter form A
PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A detective is surely following someone from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest animal of the Congo, a relative of the giraffe native to Africa.

clue.text: Tackle illicit drugs

definitions.meaning: tackle is equipment, as in fishing tackle
slang for illegal drugs, especially heroin or cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to deal with the problem of illegal drug use.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both kit or equipment and, in slang, illegal narcotics.

clue.text: Hunt missing leader, a swift seeker of prey?

indicators.note: missing leader means the word for hunt loses its first letter

parts.note: to beagle is to hunt hares with beagles

explanation.surface: A hunt has lost its master, and the hounds look round for a fast predator.
explanation.definitionFit: This large bird of prey swoops fast on its quarry, a raptor.

clue.text: Distinct delight after time with queen

indicators.note: after means the word for delight comes behind the letters for time and queen

parts.note: R stands for regina, Latin for queen
to enchant is to delight

explanation.surface: Someone is clearly delighted after spending time with the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means clear-cut and incisive, sharply defined.

clue.text: Dogmatic medical figure? One detained by agitated trainer

parts.note: doc is an informal word for a doctor

indicators.note: detained by means the letter for one is held inside the scrambled trainer
agitated suggests the letters of trainer being stirred into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A doctor is held by a nervous trainer, who turns out to be rigidly opinionated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' turns TRAINER into TRINARE; 'detained by' puts I inside it, after TRINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrinaire person applies theory rigidly, insisting on principles regardless of practicalities.
